When to reach for it:
  · Building anything that benefits from MULTIPLE specialized roles working in parallel — designer + developer + reviewer, researcher + writer + fact-checker, planner + executor + critic.

Coordination pattern: one email thread = the shared workspace. Reply-all keeps the audit trail. Use `wake` to control whose turn it is.

54	//
55	// Background bash jobs are tracked in-process so siblings bash_output / bash_kill

59	export interface BashBgJob {
60		id: string;
61		command: string;
62		cwd: string;
63		pid: number | undefined;
64		startedAt: number;
65		status: "running" | "exited" | "killed" | "failed";
66		exitCode: number | null;
67		signal: NodeJS.Signals | null;
68		logPath: string;
69		endedAt: number | undefined;
70		error: string | undefined;
71	}

73	export interface BashBgJobStore {
74		get(id: string): BashBgJob | undefined;
75		list(): BashBgJob[];
76		running(): BashBgJob[];
77		subscribe(callback: () => void): () => void;
78		kill(id: string): { job: BashBgJob | undefined; error?: string };

82	const bashBgJobs = new Map<string, BashBgJob>();
83	const bashBgSubscribers = new Set<() => void>();
84	
85	function notifyBashBgJobsChanged(): void {
86		for (const subscriber of bashBgSubscribers) subscriber();
87	}
88	
89	export function subscribeBashBgJobs(callback: () => void): () => void {
90		bashBgSubscribers.add(callback);

94	function bashBgLogDir(): string {
95		const dir = join(homedir(), ".pi", "agent", "bash-bg");
96		mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });

100	function nextBashBgId(): string {
101		return `bg_${Date.now().toString(36)}_${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`;
102	}

104	export function getBashBgJob(id: string): BashBgJob | undefined {
105		return bashBgJobs.get(id);
106	}
107	
108	export function listBashBgJobs(): BashBgJob[] {
109		return [...bashBgJobs.values()];
110	}
111	
112	export function getRunningBashBgJobsSorted(): BashBgJob[] {
113		return listBashBgJobs()
114			.filter((job) => job.status === "running")
115			.sort((a, b) => a.startedAt - b.startedAt);
116	}

118	export function killBashBgJob(id: string): { job: BashBgJob | undefined; error?: string } {
119		const job = getBashBgJob(id);
120		if (!job || job.status !== "running") return { job };
121		if (job.pid) {
122			try {
123				killProcessTree(job.pid);
124			} catch (err) {
125				return { job, error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) };
126			}
127		}
128		job.status = "killed";
129		job.endedAt = Date.now();
130		notifyBashBgJobsChanged();
131		return { job };
132	}
133	
134	export function createBashBgJobStore(): BashBgJobStore {
135		return {
136			get: getBashBgJob,
137			list: listBashBgJobs,
138			running: getRunningBashBgJobsSorted,
139			subscribe: subscribeBashBgJobs,
140			kill: killBashBgJob,
141			killAll: killAllBashBgJobs,
142		};

145	/**
146	 * Terminate every running background bash job and clear the registry.
147	 * The built-in bash-bg-jobs extension calls this on session dispose; jobs
148	 * intentionally survive extension reload because the store is process-scoped.
149	 */
150	export function killAllBashBgJobs(): void {
151		for (const job of bashBgJobs.values()) {
152			if (job.status === "running" && job.pid) {
153				try {
154					killProcessTree(job.pid);
155				} catch {
156					// best-effort; process may already be gone
157				}
158				job.status = "killed";
159				job.endedAt = Date.now();
160			}
161		}
162		bashBgJobs.clear();
163		notifyBashBgJobsChanged();
164	}

166	export function spawnBashBackground(
167		command: string,
168		cwd: string,
169		shellPath?: string,
170		commandPrefix?: string,
171	): BashBgJob {
172		const id = nextBashBgId();
173		const resolvedCommand = commandPrefix ? `${commandPrefix}\n${command}` : command;
174		const logPath = join(bashBgLogDir(), `${id}.log`);
175		const fd = openSync(logPath, "a");
176		const { shell, args } = getShellConfig(shellPath);
177		if (!existsSync(cwd)) {
178			closeSync(fd);
179			throw new Error(`Working directory does not exist: ${cwd}`);
180		}
181		const child = spawn(shell, [...args, resolvedCommand], {
182			cwd,
183			detached: process.platform !== "win32",
184			env: getShellEnv(),
185			stdio: ["ignore", fd, fd],
186		});
187		closeSync(fd);
188		if (child.pid) trackDetachedChildPid(child.pid);
189		const job: BashBgJob = {
190			id,
191			command: resolvedCommand,
192			cwd,
193			pid: child.pid,
194			startedAt: Date.now(),
195			status: "running",
196			exitCode: null,
197			signal: null,
198			logPath,
199			endedAt: undefined,
200			error: undefined,
201		};
202		bashBgJobs.set(id, job);
203		notifyBashBgJobsChanged();
204		child.on("error", (err) => {
205			job.status = "failed";
206			job.error = err.message;
207			job.endedAt = Date.now();
208			if (child.pid) untrackDetachedChildPid(child.pid);
209			notifyBashBgJobsChanged();
210		});
211		child.on("exit", (code, signal) => {
212			job.exitCode = code;
213			job.signal = signal;
214			job.endedAt = Date.now();
215			if (job.status === "running") {
216				job.status = signal ? "killed" : "exited";
217			}
218			if (child.pid) untrackDetachedChildPid(child.pid);
219			notifyBashBgJobsChanged();
220		});
221		// Don't keep the event loop alive on our behalf — caller decides.
222		child.unref();

226	/**
227	 * Adopt an already-running foreground child into the background registry instead
228	 * of killing it. Used by auto-background-on-timeout (mirrors Claude Code): the
229	 * live process keeps running, its stdout/stderr are redirected to the bg log, and
230	 * it becomes readable/killable by bgId. Callers must detach their own `onData`
231	 * listeners before calling so output isn't double-counted.
232	 */
233	function adoptBashBackground(child: ReturnType<typeof spawn>, command: string, cwd: string): BashBgJob {
234		const id = nextBashBgId();
235		const logPath = join(bashBgLogDir(), `${id}.log`);
236		const fd = openSync(logPath, "a");
237		try {
238			writeSync(fd, "[detached into background after foreground timeout \u2014 process still running]\n");
239		} catch {}
240		const append = (data: Buffer) => {
241			try {
242				writeSync(fd, data);
243			} catch {}
244		};
245		child.stdout?.on("data", append);
246		child.stderr?.on("data", append);
247		const job: BashBgJob = {
248			id,
249			command,
250			cwd,
251			pid: child.pid,
252			startedAt: Date.now(),
253			status: "running",
254			exitCode: null,
255			signal: null,
256			logPath,
257			endedAt: undefined,
258			error: undefined,
259		};
260		bashBgJobs.set(id, job);
261		notifyBashBgJobsChanged();
262		child.on("error", (err) => {
263			job.status = "failed";
264			job.error = err.message;
265			job.endedAt = Date.now();
266			try {
267				closeSync(fd);
268			} catch {}
269			if (child.pid) untrackDetachedChildPid(child.pid);
270			notifyBashBgJobsChanged();
271		});
272		child.on("exit", (code, signal) => {
273			job.exitCode = code;
274			job.signal = signal;
275			job.endedAt = Date.now();
276			if (job.status === "running") {
277				job.status = signal ? "killed" : "exited";
278			}
279			try {
280				closeSync(fd);
281			} catch {}
282			if (child.pid) untrackDetachedChildPid(child.pid);
283			notifyBashBgJobsChanged();
284		});
285		child.unref();
286		return job;
287	}

289	/**
290	 * Disposition of a foreground bash command that exceeds its timeout.
291	 *
292	 * Additive seam: the exec path stays one call deep and the policy lives in the
293	 * resolver, so the fork (or a my-pi extension) can change timeout behaviour
294	 * without reshaping the upstream exec loop. `background()` adopts the live
295	 * process into the bg registry (it keeps running); `kill()` terminates it.
296	 */
297	export interface BashTimeout {
298		readonly command: string;
299		readonly cwd: string;
300		readonly timeoutMs: number;
301		background(): BashBgJob;
302		kill(): void;
303	}
304	
305	export type BashTimeoutOutcome = { backgroundedJobId: string } | { failed: true };
306	
307	/** Upstream-faithful default: kill the timed-out process and report failure.
308	 *  Detach-on-timeout is opt-in via `onBashTimeout()` — the my-pi
309	 *  `native-tool-aliases` extension installs the detach resolver for Luke's
310	 *  `Bash` tool, so the opinionated policy lives there, not in core. */
311	function killOnBashTimeout(t: BashTimeout): BashTimeoutOutcome {
312		t.kill();
313		return { failed: true };
314	}
315	
316	let bashTimeoutResolver: (t: BashTimeout) => BashTimeoutOutcome = killOnBashTimeout;
317	
318	/**
319	 * Override what happens when a foreground bash command times out. Returns a
320	 * restore function. Consumers that choose `{ failed: true }` are responsible for
321	 * killing the process (e.g. via `t.kill()`); the default already kills.
322	 * Choose `{ backgroundedJobId }` (via `t.background()`) to detach instead.
323	 */
324	export function onBashTimeout(resolve: (t: BashTimeout) => BashTimeoutOutcome): () => void {
325		const previous = bashTimeoutResolver;
326		bashTimeoutResolver = resolve;
327		return () => {
328			bashTimeoutResolver = previous;
329		};
330	}
331	
332	/** Apply the configured timeout disposition to a still-running foreground child. */
333	function disposeBashTimeout(
334		child: ReturnType<typeof spawn>,
335		command: string,
336		cwd: string,
337		timeoutMs: number,
338	): BashTimeoutOutcome {
339		return bashTimeoutResolver({
340			command,
341			cwd,
342			timeoutMs,
343			background: () => adoptBashBackground(child, command, cwd),
344			kill: () => {
345				try {
346					child.kill("SIGKILL");
347				} catch {}
348			},
349		});
350	}
351	
352	const VERTICAL_TUI_RUN_MIN_LINES = 12;
353	// Shared byte cap for every bash-tool surface (foreground bash, background bash_output).
354	// Smaller than DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES (50KB) because shell output is the loudest single
355	// source of context bloat — and tokenjuice can rescue the full log on demand.
356	const BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES = 20 * 1024;
357	
358	function stripTrailingCarriageReturn(line: string): string {
359		return line.endsWith("\r") ? line.slice(0, -1) : line;
360	}
361	
362	function stripTerminalControls(text: string): string {
363		return stripAnsi(text)
364			.replace(/[\u0000-\u0008\u000B\u000C\u000E-\u001F\u007F]/gu, "")
365			.trimEnd();
366	}
367	
368	function isShortTerminalFragment(line: string): boolean {
369		const text = stripTrailingCarriageReturn(line);
370		return text === "" || [...text].length <= 3;
371	}
372	
373	function isLikelyWrappedTuiRun(lines: string[]): boolean {
374		if (lines.length < VERTICAL_TUI_RUN_MIN_LINES) return false;
375		const joined = lines.map(stripTrailingCarriageReturn).join("");
376		return joined.includes("\u001B") && /\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]/u.test(joined);
377	}
378	
379	function sanitizeBashBgDisplayLines(lines: string[]): string[] {
380		const sanitized: string[] = [];
381		for (let index = 0; index < lines.length; ) {
382			if (!isShortTerminalFragment(lines[index])) {
383				sanitized.push(stripTerminalControls(stripTrailingCarriageReturn(lines[index])));
384				index++;
385				continue;
386			}
387	
388			let end = index + 1;
389			while (end < lines.length && isShortTerminalFragment(lines[end])) end++;
390			const run = lines.slice(index, end);
391			if (isLikelyWrappedTuiRun(run)) {
392				const collapsed = stripTerminalControls(run.map(stripTrailingCarriageReturn).join(""));
393				if (collapsed) sanitized.push(collapsed);
394			} else {
395				for (const line of run) sanitized.push(stripTerminalControls(stripTrailingCarriageReturn(line)));
396			}
397			index = end;
398		}
399		return sanitized;
400	}
401	
402	function readBashBgLog(
403		job: BashBgJob,
404		opts: { mode: "tail" | "head" | "all"; maxLines: number },
405	): { text: string; shownLines: number; totalLines: number; truncated: boolean } {
406		let content = "";
407		try {
408			content = readFileSync(job.logPath, "utf8");
409		} catch {
410			return { text: "", shownLines: 0, totalLines: 0, truncated: false };
411		}
412		const all = content.split("\n");
413		// Trailing newline produces an empty last element; drop it.
414		if (all.length > 0 && all[all.length - 1] === "") all.pop();
415		const total = all.length;
416		const max = Math.max(1, Math.min(opts.maxLines, 1000));
417		const slice = opts.mode === "tail" ? all.slice(Math.max(0, total - max)) : all.slice(0, max);
418		const sanitized = sanitizeBashBgDisplayLines(slice).join("\n");
419		const truncation =
420			opts.mode === "tail"
421				? truncateTail(sanitized, { maxLines: max, maxBytes: BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES })
422				: truncateHead(sanitized, { maxLines: max, maxBytes: BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES });
423		const text =
424			truncation.content ||
425			(total > 0 ? `[output omitted: first line exceeds ${formatSize(BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES)}]` : "");
426		const shownLines = text ? text.split("\n").length : 0;
427		return {
428			text,
429			shownLines,
430			totalLines: total,
431			truncated: total > slice.length || truncation.truncated,
432		};
433	}

438		bgId: string;
439		pid: number | undefined;
440		logPath: string;
441		command: string;

454	/**

457	 */
458	export interface BashOperations {
459		/**
460		 * Execute a command and stream output.
461		 * @param command The command to execute
462		 * @param cwd Working directory
463		 * @param options Execution options
464		 * @returns Promise resolving to exit code (null if killed)
465		 */
466		exec: (
467			command: string,
468			cwd: string,
469			options: {
470				onData: (data: Buffer) => void;
471				signal?: AbortSignal;
472				timeout?: number;
473				env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
474			},

478	/**
479	 * Create bash operations using pi's built-in local shell execution backend.
480	 *
481	 * This is useful for extensions that intercept user_bash and still want pi's
482	 * standard local shell behavior while wrapping or rewriting commands.
483	 */
484	export function createLocalBashOperations(options?: { shellPath?: string }): BashOperations {
485		return {
486			exec: async (command, cwd, { onData, signal, timeout, env }) => {
487				const { shell, args } = getShellConfig(options?.shellPath);
488				try {
489					await fsAccess(cwd, constants.F_OK);
490				} catch {
491					throw new Error(`Working directory does not exist: ${cwd}\nCannot execute bash commands.`);
492				}
493				if (signal?.aborted) {
494					throw new Error("aborted");
495				}
496	
497				const child = spawn(shell, [...args, command], {
498					cwd,
499					detached: process.platform !== "win32",

501					stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
502					windowsHide: true,
503				});

505				let backgroundedJobId: string | undefined;
506				let timeoutHandle: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;

509				};

523					// extension adopts the live process into a background job (Claude Code
524					// parity) so long work keeps running and stays readable/killable by bgId.
525					const exitPromise = waitForChildProcess(child).then((code) => ({ kind: "exit" as const, code }));
526					const timeoutPromise =
527						timeout !== undefined && timeout > 0
528							? new Promise<{ kind: "timeout" }>((resolveTimeout) => {
529									timeoutHandle = setTimeout(() => resolveTimeout({ kind: "timeout" }), timeout * 1000);
530								})
531							: undefined;
532					const outcome = timeoutPromise ? await Promise.race([exitPromise, timeoutPromise]) : await exitPromise;
533					if (signal?.aborted) {
534						throw new Error("aborted");
535					}
536					if (outcome.kind === "timeout") {
537						// Detach the foreground listeners first so the bg log is the single sink,
538						// then hand off to the configured disposition.
539						child.stdout?.off("data", onData);
540						child.stderr?.off("data", onData);
541						const disposition = disposeBashTimeout(child, command, cwd, (timeout ?? 0) * 1000);
542						if ("backgroundedJobId" in disposition) {
543							backgroundedJobId = disposition.backgroundedJobId;
544							return { exitCode: null, backgroundedJobId };
545						}
546						// Failed disposition (the default kills): surface the timeout sentinel so
547						// the tool layer reports "Command timed out after Ns" instead of a bare exit code.
548						throw new Error(`timeout:${timeout ?? 0}`);
549					}
550					return { exitCode: outcome.code };
551				} finally {
552					// Adopted children stay tracked — the background job owns the pid now.
553					if (!backgroundedJobId && child.pid) untrackDetachedChildPid(child.pid);
554					if (timeoutHandle) clearTimeout(timeoutHandle);
555					if (signal) signal.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
556				}
557			},
558		};

709	 * literal (no escapes, no interpolation), so anything inside `'...'` cannot
710	 * be a backtick / `$()` / here-doc operator we care about. Removing them

717	/**

720	 * `<<-WORD`, `<<<` is fine — it's a here-string of literal data), and `eval`/
721	 * arithmetic substitution `$((...))` which can shell out via nested `$()`.
722	 * Returns a reason string when found, else undefined.
723	 */
724	function detectUnsafeConstructs(command: string): string | undefined {
725		const stripped = stripSingleQuoted(command);
726		if (/\$\(/.test(stripped))
727			return "command substitution `$(...)` is not permitted — inline the inner command directly";
728		if (/(^|[^\\])`/.test(stripped))
729			return "backtick command substitution is not permitted — inline the inner command directly";
730		if (/<<-?\s*['"]?\w+/.test(stripped)) return "here-doc (`<<WORD`) is not permitted — pass arguments inline instead";
731		return undefined;

734	/**
735	 * Check `command` against `policy`. Returns a human-readable reason if denied,
736	 * else undefined.
737	 *
738	 * Pipeline:
739	 *   1. Detect command substitution, backticks, here-docs — reject outright.
740	 *      These constructs let the model smuggle arbitrary commands past the
741	 *      segment scanner. A read-only explore agent never needs them.
742	 *   2. Split into pipeline/sequence segments.
743	 *   3. Multi-word patterns (e.g. "git push") match the first 1–3 tokens of
744	 *      each segment.
745	 *   4. Single-word patterns (e.g. "rm") match ANY token in any segment —
746	 *      catches `find ... | xargs rm` style chained-mutation bypasses.
747	 *   5. When `denyWrites` is set, reject unquoted `>` / `>>` / `tee` / `sponge`.
748	 */
749	export function checkBashPolicy(command: string, policy: BashPolicy): string | undefined {
750		const unsafe = detectUnsafeConstructs(command);
751		if (unsafe) {
752			return `bash policy [${policy.label}] denied: ${unsafe} (command: ${command.slice(0, 80)}). Report what you need in Open Questions instead.`;
753		}
754		const singleWordDeny = policy.denyCommands.filter((p) => !p.includes(" "));
755		const multiWordDeny = policy.denyCommands.filter((p) => p.includes(" "));
756		const segments = splitBashSegments(command);
757		for (const segment of segments) {
758			const head = firstTokens(segment);
759			for (const pattern of multiWordDeny) {
760				if (head === pattern || head.startsWith(`${pattern} `)) {
761					return `bash policy [${policy.label}] denied: "${pattern}" is not permitted (segment: ${segment.slice(0, 80)}). Report what you need in Open Questions instead.`;
762				}
763			}
764			const tokens = segment.split(/\s+/);
765			for (const token of tokens) {
766				if (singleWordDeny.includes(token)) {
767					return `bash policy [${policy.label}] denied: "${token}" is not permitted (segment: ${segment.slice(0, 80)}). Report what you need in Open Questions instead.`;
768				}
769			}
770			if (policy.denyWrites) {
771				if (/(^|[^&\d])>>?(?![&])/.test(segment) || /\btee\b/.test(segment) || /\bsponge\b/.test(segment)) {
772					return `bash policy [${policy.label}] denied: output redirection / tee is not permitted (segment: ${segment.slice(0, 80)}).`;
773				}
774			}
775		}
776		return undefined;
777	}

832	/**
833	 * Extract a quoted string starting at `startIdx` (which points at the opening quote).
834	 * Returns the unescaped content and the index just past the closing quote, or null if
835	 * the string is unterminated.
836	 */
837	function extractQuotedString(cmd: string, startIdx: number): { content: string; endIdx: number } | null {
838		const quote = cmd[startIdx];
839		if (quote !== '"' && quote !== "'") return null;
840		let i = startIdx + 1;
841		let content = "";
842		while (i < cmd.length) {
843			if (quote === '"' && cmd[i] === "\\" && i + 1 < cmd.length) {
844				content += cmd[i + 1];
845				i += 2;
846			} else if (cmd[i] === quote) {
847				return { content, endIdx: i + 1 };
848			} else {
849				content += cmd[i];

851			}

856	/**
857	 * Try to detect a heredoc embedded script in `cmd`.
858	 * Handles both quoted (`<< 'EOF'`) and unquoted (`<< EOF`) delimiters.
859	 * Returns segments or null if no heredoc found.
860	 */
861	function detectHeredoc(cmd: string): CommandSegment[] | null {
862		const heredocRe = /<<-?\s*['"]?([A-Z_][A-Z_0-9]*)['"]?\n/;
863		const match = heredocRe.exec(cmd);
864		if (!match) return null;
865		const delimiter = match[1]!;
866		const codeStart = match.index + match[0].length;
867		const closingPattern = new RegExp(`(?:^|\n)${delimiter}s*(?:\n|$)`);
868		const closeMatch = closingPattern.exec(cmd.slice(codeStart));
869		if (!closeMatch) return null;
870	
871		// Determine language from the command preceding the heredoc marker
872		const prefix = cmd.slice(0, match.index);
873		let lang = "bash";
874		for (const { pattern, lang: l } of INLINE_SCRIPT_FLAGS) {
875			if (pattern.test(`${prefix} x`)) {
876				lang = l;
877				break;
878			}
879		}
880	
881		const codeEnd = codeStart + closeMatch.index + (closeMatch[0].startsWith("\n") ? 1 : 0);
882		return [
883			{ text: cmd.slice(0, codeStart), lang: "bash" },
884			{ text: cmd.slice(codeStart, codeEnd), lang },
885			{ text: cmd.slice(codeEnd), lang: "bash" },
886		];
887	}

889	/**
890	 * Split a bash command into segments for per-language syntax highlighting.
891	 * Detects patterns like `python3 -c "..."` and heredocs.
892	 * Falls back to a single bash segment if no embedded script is found.
893	 */

895		// Try heredoc first (it uses a different delimiter style)
896		const heredocSegments = detectHeredoc(command);
897		if (heredocSegments) return heredocSegments;
898	
899		// Try inline -c/-e flag patterns
900		for (const { pattern, lang } of INLINE_SCRIPT_FLAGS) {
901			const match = pattern.exec(command);
902			if (!match) continue;
903	
904			const flagEnd = match.index + match[0].length;
905	
906			// Skip optional line-continuation whitespace between the flag and the quote
907			let quoteStart = flagEnd;
908			while (quoteStart < command.length && /[\s\\]/.test(command[quoteStart]!)) {
909				quoteStart++;
910			}
911	
912			const quoteChar = command[quoteStart];
913			if (quoteChar !== '"' && quoteChar !== "'") continue;
914	
915			const extracted = extractQuotedString(command, quoteStart);
916			if (!extracted) continue;
917	
918			// Include the opening and closing quotes in the surrounding bash segments so
919			// highlight.js sees balanced (or intentionally partial) quoting.
920			return [
921				{ text: command.slice(0, quoteStart + 1), lang: "bash" },
922				{ text: extracted.content, lang },
923				{ text: command.slice(extracted.endIdx - 1), lang: "bash" },
924			];
925		}
926	
927		return [{ text: command, lang: "bash" }];
928	}

935	function shellTokensForSimpleCommand(command: string): string[] | undefined {
936		const tokens: string[] = [];
937		let token = "";
938		let quote: '"' | "'" | undefined;
939		let escaped = false;
940	
941		for (const char of command.trim()) {
942			if (escaped) {
943				token += char;
944				escaped = false;
945				continue;
946			}
947			if (char === "\\" && quote !== "'") {
948				escaped = true;
949				continue;
950			}
951			if (quote) {
952				if (char === quote) quote = undefined;
953				else token += char;
954				continue;
955			}
956			if (char === '"' || char === "'") {
957				quote = char;
958				continue;
959			}
960			if (char === ";" || char === "|" || char === "&" || char === "\n" || char === "(" || char === ")") {
961				return undefined;
962			}
963			if (/\s/.test(char)) {
964				if (token) {
965					tokens.push(token);
966					token = "";
967				}
968				continue;
969			}
970			token += char;
971		}

973		if (token) tokens.push(token);

content.text:
`fireSessionDispose` is called only from `AgentSession.dispose()`, and `AgentSession.dispose()` is the only caller. The full picture is now clear.

---

Here are the findings for each question, with file:line evidence:

---

## Q1: When does `AgentSession.dispose()` get called?

`AgentSession.dispose()` is defined at `src/core/agent-session.ts:1147`. It is called in exactly three places:

1. **`AgentSessionRuntime.teardownCurrent()`** — `src/core/agent-session-runtime.ts:168`
   This is the private helper that runs before every top-level session replacement. It is invoked by:
   - `switchSession()` (line 199) — `ctx.switchSession()`
   - `newSession()` (line 229) — `ctx.newSession()`
   - `fork()` (lines 283, 301, 320) — `ctx.fork()` / `ctx.forkAgent` top-level branch forks
   - `importFromJsonl()` (line 364) — `/import` flow

2. **`AgentSessionRuntime.dispose()`** — `src/core/agent-session-runtime.ts:383`
   Called when the process quits (the outermost `AgentSessionRuntime` is disposed).

3. **`driveChildSession()` finally block** — `src/core/agents/executor.ts:565`
   Called unconditionally when a child-agent session finishes (success, failure, or cancellation).

`ctx.reload()` does **NOT** call `AgentSession.dispose()`. It calls `previousRunner.invalidate()` directly (`agent-session.ts:3453`) — no `disposeHandlers` fire on reload.

---

## Q2: Are separate AgentSessions created and disposed for child agents?

Yes. Every child-agent invocation (`Agent` tool, `ctx.forkAgent`, built-in `explore`/`general`/`reviewer`) creates its own fresh `AgentSession` and disposes it.

The path (`src/core/agents/executor.ts`):
- Line 660: `createAgentSessionServices(...)` — creates a **brand-new** `DefaultResourceLoader`, `settingsManager`, etc. for the child cwd.
- Line 672: `createAgentSessionFromServices(...)` — creates a new `AgentSession` with the new services.
- Line 565 (in `driveChildSession` finally block): `session.dispose()` — called unconditionally when the child finishes.

---

## Q3 (CRITICAL): Do child sessions share extension objects / `disposeHandlers`?

**No. Child agents do NOT share extension objects with the parent.** The factory is re-invoked for each child, producing entirely separate `Extension` objects with separate `disposeHandlers` arrays.

The chain:

1. `createAgentSessionServices()` (`agent-session-services.ts:133`) creates a **new `DefaultResourceLoader`** via `new DefaultResourceLoader(...)` (line 141) and calls `resourceLoader.reload()` (line 147).
2. `reload()` (`resource-loader.ts:403`) calls `loadExtensions(extensionRequests, ...)` (line 481), which calls `loadExtension()` for each extension path, which calls `loadExtensionModule(resolvedPath)` and then `await factory(api)` (`loader.ts:723`). The factory runs again.
3. `createExtension()` (`loader.ts:679`) creates a new `Extension` object with a fresh `disposeHandlers: []` array (line 697).
4. The `api` passed to the factory is a new `ExtensionAPI` bound to this new `Extension` object (`loader.ts:722`). Any `ctx.onSessionDispose(handler)` call in the factory pushes to **this new extension's `disposeHandlers`**, not the parent's.
5. The child's `AgentSession._buildRuntime()` (`agent-session.ts:3417`) creates a **new `ExtensionRunner`** wrapping those new extension objects.

Therefore `fireSessionDispose()` on child disposal iterates the child's own `disposeHandlers` — a completely separate array from the parent's. The parent's handlers are **not affected**.

For `.ts` extensions (jiti path), `moduleCache: false` (`loader.ts:660`) ensures the module itself is not cached either. For pre-compiled `.js/.mjs` extensions (native `import()`, line 651), the ES module **is** cached by the runtime — the same factory function reference is returned — but `factory(api)` is still called again with a new `api` and new `Extension` object each time. Module-level singleton state in the factory (closures, module-scoped variables) would be shared, but the `Extension` object and its `disposeHandlers` are always new.

---

## Q4: Are `disposeHandlers` ever cleared/reset?

**Never.** `fireSessionDispose()` (`runner.ts:636–651`) iterates `ext.disposeHandlers` and calls each handler, but does **not** clear the array afterward. The handlers persist for the lifetime of the `Extension` object.

However, this is not a problem in practice: each `AgentSession` holds its own `ExtensionRunner` wrapping its own `Extension` objects. Once `session.dispose()` finishes, the session and its runner are discarded (the runner is invalidated at line 1162 of `agent-session.ts`). The extension objects and their `disposeHandlers` become unreachable. There is no case where the same `Extension` object lives across two `AgentSession` instances — child sessions always get fresh objects (Q3 above), and top-level session replacements rebuild the runtime via `createRuntime()` which calls `createAgentSessionServices()` → new `resourceLoader.reload()` → new extension objects.

---

## Practical Answer

If extension X registers one `onSessionDispose` handler during its factory call:

- **Top-level session replacement** (`newSession`, `switchSession`, `fork`, `importFromJsonl`): fires the handler exactly once on the outgoing session's `AgentSession.dispose()`.
- **Process quit**: fires the handler once on the final `AgentSessionRuntime.dispose()`.
- **Child/sub-agent completion** (`Agent` tool, `ctx.forkAgent`, built-ins): does **NOT** fire the parent session's handler. The child has its own extension objects; its `session.dispose()` fires the child's `disposeHandlers`. The parent's handler is untouched.
- **`ctx.reload()`**: does **NOT** fire `disposeHandlers` at all (calls `invalidate()` directly).

So the answer to your practical question is **(a)**: the handler fires only on top-level session replacement events (and process quit), not on child-agent completions. The same single handler will re-fire on each top-level session replacement for the life of the process, since the parent's `Extension` object and its `disposeHandlers` array persist across replacements and are never cleared.

content.text:
Empirically confirmed — the bug is real:

```
0. baseline (no extension)            : KILL ❌   ← core default
1. after activate (session A start)   : DETACH ✅  ← works initially
2. after dispose A (NO new session)   : KILL ❌   ← dispose tears down the resolver
3. after activate (session B start)   : DETACH ✅  ← only a fresh activation restores it
4. after double-dispose (stacked)     : KILL ❌   ← stacked restores clobber to kill
```

`restoreBashTimeout()` in `onSessionDispose` reverts the process-global detach resolver to kill. Since it's a single package-global and the restores aren't a real stack, any dispose (/new, /fork, switchSession) leaves a window — and the stacked-restore case clobbers to kill outright. The detach policy is a stable process-wide preference; it shouldn't be torn down per session. Let me apply the fix.

lines: // Code-style auto-background: a timed-out command keeps running as a bg job,
// readable via TaskOutput and stoppable via TaskStop. `t.background()` adopts
// the live process into the same bg registry these tools already read.
+  // Install once as a process-wide preference and NEVER restore it on session
+  // dispose. `onBashTimeout` mutates a single package-global resolver, and its
+  // restore fns are not a real stack — restoring on every top-level dispose
+  // (/new, /fork, switchSession) reverted the global to the core kill policy,
+  // so a timed-out command was KILLED instead of detached until the next session
+  // re-activated this extension (and stacked disposes clobbered it to kill
+  // outright). The policy is idempotent — always the same detach closure — so
+  // re-installing on each activation and never restoring keeps auto-background

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Bash auto-background + monitoring**: "get the bash auto background functionality working and monitoring to trigger nicely in my pi fork and extensions." Reference UX provided via a Claude Code transcript (auto-background a long bash command on timeout, arm a monitor, get woken on completion). Via AskUserQuestion, Luke clarified the gap is: **"Auto-bg not firing live"** (timed-out commands getting killed instead of detaching at runtime) AND **"Wired — verify e2e"** (verify the full flow works in real pi, fix whatever breaks). Luke did NOT select the "bg completion → wake me" option, so the wake-on-bg-completion bridge is explicitly OUT of scope.
   - **Footer/statusline**: "get my footer tui nice and dynamic like claude code." Via AskUserQuestion, Luke chose **"Full statusline restyle"** (rework footer layout/segments/colors to match Claude Code's look).
   - **Footer constraint (verbatim)**: "don't remove any of my nice stuff in the footer / statusline" — footer work must be ADDITIVE; remove no existing segments.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Pi fork architecture: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (core, patch only for generic primitives) vs `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions` (customize here first). Rule from pi-dev.md.
   - `onBashTimeout(resolve)` seam in core `bash.ts`: sets a single module-global `bashTimeoutResolver`; returns a restore fn. Core default = `killOnBashTimeout`; detach is opt-in.
   - `adoptBashBackground` / `BashBgJob` registry (module-global `bashBgJobs` Map in bash.ts) — auto-detach adopts the live process into a bg job readable via TaskOutput, killable via TaskStop.
   - Extension lifecycle: default export factory runs ONCE per process; reused across runners via `getExtensionsForRunner()`. `onSessionDispose` handlers stored on extension object's `disposeHandlers` array, fired by `fireSessionDispose()` (runner.ts:636) from `AgentSession.dispose()` (agent-session.ts:1147). Dispose triggers: top-level `/new`/`/fork`/`switchSession` (via `teardownCurrent` agent-session-runtime.ts:168), process quit. NOT child-agent completion (fresh extension objects), NOT `ctx.reload()`.
   - Agent wake path: `pi.sendMessage(msg, opts)` → `sendCustomMessage` (agent-session.ts:1943) → if idle+triggerTurn → `_runAgentPrompt`; if streaming → `agent.steer`/`agent.followUp`; `deliverAs: "nextTurn"` queues.
   - `agentLoopContinue` (agent-loop.ts:64) throws "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" if last message role is "assistant".
   - my-pi gates: `test:extension-gate:ci` (chain of smoke scripts in package.json), `test:extension-gate` (= ci + prompt-health:live). Fork gate: `test:build-gate`.
   - Footer: extension `setStatus(key, text)` segments (sorted alphabetically), `renderBackgroundStatusLine` (footer pills via `getRegisteredFooters()`), token/cache/cost/context computed in `getUsageTotals`.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **`~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts`** (THE FIX):
     - Why: installs the detach-on-timeout resolver; the bug was here.
     - Change 1 (~line 248-258): replaced `const restoreBashTimeout = isEnabled("bash") ? onBashTimeout(...) : () => {};` with an idempotent install-and-never-restore:
       ```js
       // Install once as a process-wide preference and NEVER restore it on session
       // dispose. ... Regression: autobg-lifecycle.test.mjs.
       if (isEnabled("bash")) {
         onBashTimeout((t) => ({ backgroundedJobId: t.background().id }));
       }
       ```
     - Change 2 (~line 309): removed `restoreBashTimeout();` from the dispose handler, leaving:
       ```js
       pi.onSessionDispose(() => {
         jobs.killAll();
       });
       ```
   - **`~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/autobg-lifecycle.test.mjs`** (NEW, regression test):
     - Why: locks in the fix; would have failed pre-fix (step "after session dispose" returned "kill").
     - Uses jiti to load index.ts factory against a stub api, captures disposeHandler; probes resolver state by running `bash.execute("p", {command:"sleep 3", timeout:1})` — "detach" if output contains "detached into background job", "kill" if rejects with "timed out after". Asserts: baseline=kill, after-activate=detach, after-dispose(no reactivate)=detach, after-stacked-disposes=detach. Passes.
   - **`~/Projects/personal/my-pi/package.json`**:
     - Added script: `"test:native-tool-overrides:autobg": "node extensions/native-tool-overrides/autobg-lifecycle.test.mjs",`
     - Inserted into `test:extension-gate:ci`: `... && npm run test:native-tool-overrides:smoke && npm run test:native-tool-overrides:autobg && npm run test:time-context:smoke && ...`
   - **`~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts`** (read only, 1676 lines): the seam — `onBashTimeout`, `adoptBashBackground`, `disposeBashTimeout`, `createLocalBashOperations` (timeout → `disposeBashTimeout` → resolver), `spawnBashBackground`, bg job registry.
   - **`~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts`** (read only): `sendCustomMessage` (1943-2047, handles triggerTurn/steer/followUp/nextTurn; catch at 2030 only falls back to steer on "already processing"); `_runAgentPrompt` (1555-1568, post-run loop `while(_handlePostAgentRun()) await agent.continue()`); `_handlePostAgentRun` (1570-1600); sendMessage binding (3076, 4148).
   - **`~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts`** (read only): throws "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" at lines 75 and 132.
   - **`~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/monitor/index.ts`** (read only, 1055 lines): wake via `safeSend(pi, {customType:"monitor-event",...}, {deliverAs:"steer", triggerTurn:true})` in exit handler (line ~819) and `flushNotify` (line ~361). `updateFooter` (line 311) uses `ctx.ui.setStatus("monitor", "● N monitors · ↓ or alt+m")`. Smoke test passes.
   - **`~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts`** (read only, 354 lines, for Task #4): `FooterComponent.render(width)` — line 1 = pwd·branch·session; line 2 = token stats (↑↓RW), cache% (color-coded by steadyState), cost, t{turns}, context% + model·thinking (right-aligned); then `renderBackgroundStatusLine` (extension footer pills, line 116/336); then extension statuses (line 342). NO spinner/elapsed/running-shell indicator currently.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Module resolution failure**: `/tmp/autobg-repro.mjs` couldn't resolve `jiti`/`@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent` from /tmp. # Pi Development — Router

## Core rule

- Customize Pi via `~/Projects/personal/my-pi` extensions/packages first.
- Patch `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` core only for generic platform primitives that cannot be exposed through existing hooks/filters.
- If core changes are unavoidable, log them in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` and run the fork + extension gates.

## Read when

| Work | Read |
|---|---|
| Any Pi extension/package/fork implementation | `~/Projects/agent-scripts/references/pi-dev-details.md` |
| Prompt-cache, `tools[]`, system prompt, `forkAgent`, child agents, memory extractors | skill `pi-cache-stability` + `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` |
| Extension API / examples | `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md` |
| Runtime/package inventory | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` |
| Setup/runtime registry changes | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-setup/` catalog YAML; generated files are scanner-owned |
| Config settings / env layering | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/config-layering.md` |
| Release/versioning/rollback | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` |

## Hot paths

- Core fork: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (`packages/coding-agent` for agent loop/tools/docs).
- Extension lab: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/`.
- Full profile: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/packages/my-pi-full/package.json`.

- Model metadata: `~/.pi/agent/models.json`; Opus 4.8 is `claude-bridge/claude-opus-4-8`.

## Cache footguns

- Keep `params.system` and `tools[]` byte-stable across same-cwd sessions.
- Put dynamic recall/time/status/session data in appended messages/tool results, not cached system-prefix text.
- Mark situational/heavy extension tools `deferLoading: true`; gate with `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:deferred-tool-contracts`.
- Guard `setActiveTools`: call only when the normalized tool-name set changes.
- Prefer `tool_reference` / provider-native `defer_loading` over mutating active tools after `tool_search`.

## Gates

- Extension/profile/cache surface: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`.
- Fork/core surface: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`.

All four tasks done. Summary:

## Done

**Bash auto-background (Tasks #1–2)** — root-caused the "not firing live" bug to `restoreBashTimeout()` in `native-tool-overrides`'s `onSessionDispose`: it reverted the *process-global* detach resolver back to core's kill policy on every `/new`/`/fork`/`switchSession`, and stacked disposes clobbered it permanently. Fixed with install-once / never-restore. Regression test `autobg-lifecycle.test.mjs` drives the real factory through activate→dispose→stacked-dispose with a genuine 1s-timeout `sleep` and asserts the policy stays "detach"; wired into `test:extension-gate:ci`.

**Monitoring e2e (Task #3)** — wake path verified at code level (`pi.sendMessage` → `sendCustomMessage` honors `triggerTurn`/`deliverAs:"steer"`), smoke passes. One historical wake failed with `Cannot continue from message role: assistant` (2026-05-19) — that's a rare core agent-loop fragility in the post-run `agent.continue()` loop, shared with idle-return, **not** a monitor-wiring bug. Surfacing it as a noted finding rather than speculative core surgery (matches your "verify e2e" scope). Worth a follow-up if you want me to add a trailing-assistant guard.

**Footer (Task #4)** — added a **streaming work-bar** to the bottom statusline: pulsing dot + elapsed timer on the left, `esc to interrupt` on the right, shown only while a turn streams. This is the Claude-Code "liveness" pi's footer lacked (pi's spinner sits *above* the editor). # Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Session picker badges sessions that are open in another live pi process, backed by a `session-liveness` probe.

### Fixed

- Agent tool call and collapsed result rendering now show provider/model and thinking metadata.
- Agent tool call labels inherit the parent session's live model and thinking level via a new engine `snapshot()`, so forked agent calls render the active provider/model/thinking instead of stale defaults.
- Stubbed `sessionLiveness` in the #5080 shutdown ordering regression test so its mock matches `shutdown()` now calling `this.sessionLiveness.stop()`.
- Reset the footer assistant turn count after compaction by rendering it from the same post-compaction transcript window as token/cache totals.
- Replaced a negated-OR null guard with optional chaining (`!adapter?.kill`) in `core/tools/background-tasks.ts`. Behavior-preserving.
